text:
maria: Hey team — noticed a p95 decode bump (~35ms) after the kernel-selection tweak on canary. Attaching quick flamegraph link and a couple of perf snippets.

profiler-bot: Auto-flamegraph generated: https://profiler.internal/runs/hostframe-abc123 — top host time: parse/tokenize 42%, grpc handling 16%, kernel_dispatch 12%.

sam: Can you repro locally or is it only on canary? which workload?

maria: Repros on perf-harness chat-long-history. Quick `perf report` excerpt:
```
Samples: 1000  | parse_token       420  42%
Samples: 1000  | grpc_handler      160  16%
Samples: 1000  | kv_lookup         100  10%
```

eli: Two observations from traces: (1) Many tiny streaming chunks are causing gRPC per-message overhead, and (2) KV cache hit rate dropped (96% -> 68%) because keys include varying session prefixes. Host CPU is dominated by tokenization + parse.

cheng: Quick mitigation ideas: coalesce small incoming chunks at ingress, and normalize KV prefixes before cache lookup. That should reduce host-side syscalls and increase kv hit rate.

cheng: Proposed ingress config (proto):
```yaml
ingress:
  coalesce_threshold_ms: 8
  coalesce_max_bytes: 4096
  max_chunks_before_batch: 6
  normalize_kv_prefix: true
```

sam: Any microbench numbers on that?

maria: Local microbench — coalesce only: host parse CPU -18%, p95 reduced by ~22ms. With kv-normalize applied we recovered hit rate to ~94% and reduced kv_lookup cost.

eli: Another longer-term idea: pre-tokenize at the edge for non-streaming requests so the hot host thread does less tokenization. For streaming keep incremental tokenization to preserve low-latency streaming.

sam: Caveat: pre-tokenize changes batching shapes and increases ingress memory and network payload. We'll need to measure batching heuristics impact.

maria: I'm going to run a canary with coalesce + kv-normalize only (no pre-tokenize) to isolate effects.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: canary/hostframe-coalesce-kvnorm (id: canary-237) — rolling 5% traffic.

sam: Metrics to watch during canary: ingress_parse_cpu, grpc_p99, tokens_per_second, kv_hit_rate, request_tail_latency, kernel_dispatch_time.

maria: Will post results in ~30m. If stable, we'll spin up canary-2 adding pre-tokenize and compare.

eli: Also added a tracing span `tokenize_shard` so we can attribute hot threads in flamegraphs.

maria: Added as well. Quick note: in profiler output I saw a lot of short-lived goroutines in host parser — might be an allocation pattern we can optimize later.

cheng: I'll draft a minimal patch for coalescing with an opt-out flag and a unit test for chunk boundaries.

maria: Assigning follow-ups: @cheng patch, @eli tracing span instrumentation, @sam define canary SLOs and rollback thresholds. :thumbsup:

sam: Ack. Suggest rollback if grpc_p99 > baseline + 30ms or kv_hit_rate drops below 90%.

profiler-bot: Reminder: include `flamegraph --collapse-threads` on next run to make host thread hotspots clearer.

maria: Thanks everyone — will report back. Short summary: coalesce + kv-normalize looks promising; next steps A/B pre-tokenize and refine batching heuristics.

maria: closing thread for now, will reopen if regressions show up or canary fails.
